## English

My research asks how the movement of people across national borders is entangled with social stratification and inequality: how many people moved, from where to where, and who they were; where they stood in the society they left; and where they and their children ended up in the one they joined. In recent years in particular, my work has covered both people who leave Japan and people who come to it, from the Japanese who moved to the United States in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries to Japanese living abroad and immigrants living in Japan today.

```{=html}

<figure><a href="/assets/research/fig_japanese_abroad_2025.png" class="lightbox" data-gallery="research-en"><img src="/assets/research/thumb_map2025.jpg" alt="A world map with red circles showing the number of Japanese nationals living in each country in 2025." loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>Japanese living abroad by country or area, 2025 (source: made by the author from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs’ <em>Annual Report of Statistics on Japanese Nationals Overseas</em>)</figcaption></figure>
</div>
<div class="fig-row-caption">
<p>In both maps the area of each circle is proportional to the number of residents, and the 2025 map is drawn to roughly the same scale as the 1922 map. Hawaii has its own circle in 1922 and is counted in the United States in 2025. The 1922 map is the plate “Japanese from Japan proper living abroad” (30 June 1922) in the yearbook compiled by the Cabinet Bureau of Statistics. The 2025 figures are as of 1 October 2025, and the map data are from Natural Earth.</p>
</div>
```

I approach these questions with the tools of historical and social demography and analyze data within interpretive frameworks that are meaningful for the social sciences. Much of the work consists of assembling population data of different kinds, assessing their representativeness, and harmonizing them, and sometimes of producing them. For my historical research, this means administrative and census records from the first half of the twentieth century, linked across years and sometimes across sources to follow the same people over time. For contemporary research, it means archived social survey microdata, and I have also taken part in conducting surveys: as a member of the research group for the [2025 SSM Survey](https://ssm2025.jp/) I work on its [survey of foreign residents](https://ssm2025.jp/survey_d/), and in another collaborative survey in the Tokyo metropolitan area I have carried out qualitative follow-up interviews with respondents to its quantitative survey.

```{=html}
<p class="fig-hint">Click an image to enlarge.</p>
<div class="fig-row fig-row-3">
<figure><a href="/assets/research/census_1940_sacramento.jpg" class="lightbox" data-gallery="research-en"><img src="/assets/research/thumb_census1940_tall.jpg" alt="Handwritten 1940 census entries: relation, sex, race recorded as Jp, age, and birthplace such as Japan or California." loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>A page of the 1940 U.S. census, Sacramento, California (source: <a href="https://catalog.archives.gov/id/126100278">U.S. National Archives</a>, public domain)</figcaption></figure>
<figure><a href="/assets/research/wra_form26.jpg" class="lightbox" data-gallery="research-en"><img src="/assets/research/thumb_wra_tall.jpg" alt="Upper left part of a blank Individual Record form (Form WRA-26) of the War Relocation Authority." loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>The War Relocation Authority’s individual record form (source: <a href="https://catalog.archives.gov/id/1264228">U.S. National Archives</a>, documentation for Record Group 210, public domain)</figcaption></figure>
<figure><a href="/assets/research/jarp_box.jpg" class="lightbox" data-gallery="research-en"><img src="/assets/research/thumb_jarp_box.jpg" alt="A gray archive box standing on a table, labeled UCLA Library, Department of Special Collections, Collection 1575, Levine, Gene N., JARP - survey forms, Box 1." loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>A box containing individual records of JARP, a historical Japanese American social survey from the 1960s (source: photo by the author, Collection 1575, UCLA Library Special Collections)</figcaption></figure>
</div>
<div class="fig-row-caption">
<p>Census records from 1920 to 1940, linked so that the same people can be followed over time, are the data for my article in <em><a href="https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ssresearch.2026.103442">Social Science Research</a></em>. Records made with the form of the War Relocation Authority, which incarcerated Japanese Americans during World War II, are the source for my article in the <em><a href="https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/1369183X.2021.1963219">Journal of Ethnic and Migration Studies</a></em>, and the JARP survey is the data source for my article in <em><a href="https://read.dukeupress.edu/demography/article/doi/10.1215/00703370-11370115/387961/Social-Mobility-Across-the-Pacific-An-Analysis-of?guestAccessKey=daafe79a-b043-467a-8674-f67e0f035638">Demography</a></em>.</p>
<details><summary>Notes</summary>
<p>The census page includes Japanese American households (“Jp” in the race column); names are masked in the full page. The U.S. government releases census records to the public <a href="https://www.census.gov/about/history/census-records-family-history/census-records/72-year-rule.html">72 years after each census</a>, and as a record of the federal government the page is in the public domain. The individual record form is Form WRA-26. The Japanese American Research Project (JARP) surveyed Japanese immigrants and their descendants in the continental United States in the 1960s. The box shown is labeled “Collection 1575, Levine, Gene N., JARP - survey forms, Box 1”; the printed details on the request slip attached to it are masked. I visited the archive to check some coding practices that are not documented in the data files available online.</p>
</details>
</div>
```

My current research, supported in part by a [JSPS Grant-in-Aid for Early-Career Scientists](https://kaken.nii.ac.jp/en/grant/KAKENHI-PROJECT-26K16547/) (FY2026–2029), extends this work, which began with the Japanese who settled in the continental United States, to people from Japan who settled in other countries, and pursues the same questions among immigrants in Japan today.

My publications are listed on the [Publications](/publications/) page.

## 日本語

研究の軸にあるのは，国境を越える人の移動が社会階層とどう結びついているのか，という問いである．どれだけの人が，どこからどこへ動き，それはどのような人々なのか．出身社会の階層のどこから来て，移動先で本人と子どもはどのような地位に就くのか．特に近年は，明治・大正期に米国へ渡った日系移民から，現在海外で暮らす日本人と日本で暮らす外国人移民まで，日本から出ていく人々と日本に来る人々の双方を主な研究対象としている．

```{=html}
<p class="fig-hint">画像をクリックすると拡大する．</p>
<div class="fig-row fig-row-2">
<figure><a href="/assets/research/map_1922_zairyu_naichijin.jpg" class="lightbox" data-gallery="research-ja"><img src="/assets/research/thumb_map1922.jpg" alt="「海外在留内地人（大正十一年六月三十日）」と題した1922年の世界地図．" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>国・地域別にみた海外在留の日本人，1922年（出典：内閣統計局編『第42回 日本帝国統計年鑑』東京統計協会，1924年．画像は一橋大学経済研究所「<a href="https://d-infra.ier.hit-u.ac.jp/Japanese/govstat-database/">公的統計テキストデータベース</a>」提供）</figcaption></figure>
<figure><a href="/assets/research/fig_japanese_abroad_2025.png" class="lightbox" data-gallery="research-ja"><img src="/assets/research/thumb_map2025.jpg" alt="2025年の国・地域別の海外在留邦人数を赤い円で示した世界地図．" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>国・地域別にみた海外在留の日本人，2025年（出典：外務省領事局政策課「海外在留邦人数調査統計」（2025年10月1日現在）をもとに筆者作成）</figcaption></figure>
</div>
<div class="fig-row-caption">
<p>2枚とも円の面積は在留者数に比例し，2025年の図は1922年の図とほぼ同じ縮尺で描いてある．ハワイは，1922年の図では独立した円で示され，2025年の図では米国に含まれる．1922年の図は「海外在留内地人（大正十一年六月三十日）」と題した図版である．2025年の図は2025年10月1日現在の人数で，地図データは Natural Earth による．</p>
</div>
```

研究方法としては，計量社会学と歴史・社会人口学のアプローチを採用し，種類の異なる人口データを集めて，代表性を検討し，比較できる形に整え，時には自ら調査してデータを作ったうえで，社会科学的に意味のある解釈枠組みのもとで分析している．例えば，歴史上の移民については，20世紀前半の行政記録や国勢調査の個票を年をまたいで連結し，同じ人物を追えるようにする．現在の移民についてはアーカイブされた社会調査データの個票を用いるだけでなく，社会調査の実施にも加わってきた．[2025年SSM調査](https://ssm2025.jp/)では研究会メンバーとして[外国籍住民調査](https://ssm2025.jp/survey_d/)に携わり，首都圏の別の共同調査では量的調査の回答者への事後的なインタビュー調査も担ってきた．

```{=html}
<p class="fig-hint">画像をクリックすると拡大する．</p>
<div class="fig-row fig-row-3">
<figure><a href="/assets/research/census_1940_sacramento.jpg" class="lightbox" data-gallery="research-ja"><img src="/assets/research/thumb_census1940_tall.jpg" alt="1940年国勢調査の手書きの記入．続柄，性別，人種欄の「Jp」，年齢，出生地（Japan や California）．" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>1940年の米国国勢調査の個票（出典：<a href="https://catalog.archives.gov/id/126100278">米国国立公文書館</a>，パブリックドメイン）</figcaption></figure>
<figure><a href="/assets/research/wra_form26.jpg" class="lightbox" data-gallery="research-ja"><img src="/assets/research/thumb_wra_tall.jpg" alt="戦時転住局の個人記録の様式（Form WRA-26）の左上の部分．未記入．" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>戦時転住局の個人記録の様式（出典：<a href="https://catalog.archives.gov/id/1264228">米国国立公文書館</a>，Record Group 210 の技術文書，パブリックドメイン）</figcaption></figure>
<figure><a href="/assets/research/jarp_box.jpg" class="lightbox" data-gallery="research-ja"><img src="/assets/research/thumb_jarp_box.jpg" alt="机の上に立てた灰色の資料箱．ラベルに「UCLA Library, Department of Special Collections, Collection 1575, Levine, Gene N., JARP - survey forms, Box 1」とある．" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>1960年代の日系人社会調査（JARP）の個票を収めた資料箱（出典：筆者撮影，Collection 1575, UCLA Library Special Collections）</figcaption></figure>
</div>
<div class="fig-row-caption">
<p>1920年から1940年の国勢調査の個票を連結し，同じ人物を追えるようにしたパネルデータが，<em><a href="https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ssresearch.2026.103442">Social Science Research</a></em> 掲載論文の資料である．第二次世界大戦中に日系人を収容した戦時転住局（War Relocation Authority）がこの様式で作った記録が <em><a href="https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/1369183X.2021.1963219">Journal of Ethnic and Migration Studies</a></em> 掲載論文の資料であり，JARP のデータが <em><a href="https://read.dukeupress.edu/demography/article/doi/10.1215/00703370-11370115/387961/Social-Mobility-Across-the-Pacific-An-Analysis-of?guestAccessKey=daafe79a-b043-467a-8674-f67e0f035638">Demography</a></em> 掲載論文の資料である．</p>
<details><summary>注</summary>
<p>国勢調査の個票はカリフォルニア州サクラメントのもので，日系人の世帯が含まれる（人種欄の「Jp」）．全体画像では氏名を伏せた．米国政府は国勢調査の個票を<a href="https://www.census.gov/about/history/census-records-family-history/census-records/72-year-rule.html">調査の72年後に公開</a>しており，この個票は連邦政府の記録であり，パブリックドメインである．個人記録の様式は Form WRA-26 である．Japanese American Research Project（JARP）は，1960年代に米国本土の日系移民とその子孫を対象に行われた社会調査である．写真の箱のラベルには「Collection 1575, Levine, Gene N., JARP - survey forms, Box 1」とある．箱に差し込まれた請求票の記載は伏せた．オンラインで公開されているデータファイルには，コーディングの方法が文書に残されていない箇所があり，その一部を確かめるためにこの資料を閲覧した．</p>
</details>
</div>
```

現在は[科研費若手研究](https://kaken.nii.ac.jp/ja/grant/KAKENHI-PROJECT-26K16547/)（2026〜2029年度）などにより，米国を中心とした研究をより多様な国・地域に広げるとともに，現代の日本で暮らす移民にも関心を向けている．

業績は [Publications](/publications/) のページにまとめている．
